title: perf(canary): auto-detection of latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Priya Natarajan
body:
Motivation: Production canaries are currently manually configured and rely on static thresholds, which has led to missed regressions and noisy rollouts. This PR adds an automated detector that continuously monitors per-route latency and throughput on canaries, calculates dynamic baselines, and triggers rollout guards (pause / rollback / traffic hold) when statistically significant regressions are detected.

Summary of changes: Implemented a canary detector service (perf/canary/detector.py) that consumes rolling-window statistics from the serving runtime, computes expected distributions per model/route, and runs a lightweight statistical test (Welch's t-test with Bonferroni correction and configurable hysteresis) across latency P50/P90/P99 and throughput/success-rate metrics. Added rollout guard logic (perf/canary/rollout_guard.py) with three actions: PAUSE (stop traffic shifts), HOLD (keep canary at current weight and open escalation), and ROLLBACK (automatic revert to previous stable variant). Hooked detectors into the Console alerts and to the existing rollout controller so failures surface in dashboards and Linear tickets.

Backward compatibility & safety: All behavior is behind the feature flag "perf.canary_autodetect" (deploy default: off). The detector falls back to static thresholds if historical data is insufficient. Actions require either: (a) auto-rollback enabled OR (b) manual approval from a configured set of approvers. Hysteresis settings are configurable per-environment and include a minimum sample size, minimum observation window, and minimum relative regression to avoid noise-driven actions.

Observability & telemetry: Added new metric names and tags: canary_detector.latency.{p50,p90,p99}.regression_score, canary_detector.throughput.regression_score, canary_detector.alerts_total (labels: route, model, canary_id, action). Dashboards: perf/canary/dashboards.json (panels for rolling baselines, recent alerts, and action history). Traces: added tracing spans around detection decision paths for sampling and debugging.

Testing: Unit tests for detector logic (tests/perf/test_canary_detection.py) including synthetic regressions and low-sample scenarios. Integration harness: small load job in perf-canary lab that exercises traffic shifting + simulated regression to validate guard actions. Perf regression suite was run twice because of an initial flaky synthetic generator; final run shows no measurable p50 regression on our baseline workloads.

Rollout plan: Feature-flag rollout in 3 steps: (1) enable detection in internal staging with auto-actions disabled, (2) enable on 5% canary traffic for internal services with manual approval path, (3) enable auto-rollback for a subset of low-risk routes (non-customer-facing batch endpoints) after 1 week of stable telemetry.

Checklist: - [x] Detector core algorithm implemented - [x] Rollout guard actions wired into rollout controller - [x] Metrics + dashboards added - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Feature flag gating and config knobs - [x] Documentation (docs/perf/canary.md)

Notes: See linked Linear items ENG-4321 (canary detector MVP) and ENG-4387 (rollout guard integration). This PR intentionally keeps statistical test lightweight to avoid CPU overhead in the runtime path; all heavy aggregation runs in the detector service which is horizontally scalable.

Potential follow-ups: - Add anomaly-detection ML model as an optional detector backend - Expose per-tenant sensitivity tuning in Console - Add canary-specific synthetic load profiles to the perf lab

review_comments: Marco Li (2026-01-16): Nice work. Two questions: 1) how are you handling low-sample routes (few requests per minute)? 2) can we avoid adding more hot path CPU? Please add knobs for minimum sample size and move heavy aggregation off-path.

Priya Natarajan (2026-01-16): Reply: Added min_sample_size and min_window config; detector only uses pre-aggregated metrics from the metrics-aggregator stream to avoid runtime CPU impact. Updated docs with details.
Anika Shah (2026-01-17): Please add an option to require manual approval before auto-rollback for high-risk routes. Also suggest exposing the regression_score in the Console UI for operators.
Priya Natarajan (2026-01-17): Reply: Added per-route 'auto_rollback' flag and Console exposure for regression_score. Marked high-risk routes via label in rollout controller.
Rafael Torres (2026-01-19): I saw a flaky perf test on first CI run (synthetic generator timing). Can you stabilize or mark the test as non-flaky?
Priya Natarajan (2026-01-19): Reply: Fixed the synthetic generator seeding and added retry logic in the integration harness. Re-ran perf suite; final result green.

release_notes: Added an automated canary detector that computes dynamic baselines for latency and throughput and provides rollout guards (pause/hold/rollback). Feature gated behind perf.canary_autodetect. New metrics and dashboards added for observability.
